text:
jess_support: Hey team — escalated issue from AcmeCorp: multiple 502/timeout failures on generation endpoint. Customer provided a sample request_id: req_20250202_0a7f9c. They say it happened ~2025-02-02T18:12:34Z and affects ~15% of calls for that minute.

sara_support: Can we get someone to look up server-side traces/logs for that request_id? Customer included a curl but we need internal logs and if possible the route/host it hit.

anil_eng: I can take a look. Do we have full request_id? the one you pasted looks truncated. Full string would help (often contains region shard). If they only gave the short id we can still search by prefix.

jess_support: They sent the header value exactly as: req_20250202_0a7f9c. Here's their curl (sanitized):
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" -H "X-Request-ID: req_20250202_0a7f9c" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"input":"hello"}' \
  "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate"
```

marco_sre: OK pulling logs. For quick look: Elasticsearch (Kibana) index is prod-requests-*. Example query I run: 
```
POST /prod-requests-*/_search
{
  "query": {
    "term": { "request_id.keyword": "req_20250202_0a7f9c" }
  },
  "sort": [{ "@timestamp": "desc" }],
  "size": 200
}
```
This returns any entries we have up to retention window. Note: prod request logs are retained 21 days. If the event is older than that we only have traces in APM (retained 90 days).

marco_sre: If you're using Loki/Promtail we also have a Loki example: 
```
{job="redwood-api"} |= "req=\"req_20250202_0a7f9c\"" | sort_desc() | limit 200
```

anil_eng: I queried Kibana and found 6 hits between 2025-02-02T18:12:33Z and 18:12:35Z. Top-level errors: 3 entries with upstream timeout to model-worker-3 (504) and one 502 from gateway while streaming. Attaching the pared-down lines: 
```
"@timestamp": "2025-02-02T18:12:33.801Z", "request_id": "req_20250202_0a7f9c", "host": "api-01.prod.redwood", "route": "/v1/generate", "status": 504, "upstream": "model-worker-3", "dur_ms": 31000
"@timestamp": "2025-02-02T18:12:34.102Z", "request_id": "req_20250202_0a7f9c", "host": "api-02.prod.redwood", "route": "/v1/generate", "status": 502, "proxy_err": "bad gateway"
```

jess_support: Thanks — can you confirm whether this is a transient worker overload or something systemic? Customer reports 15% of calls in that minute failed.

marco_sre: Looks like worker-side timeouts. The 31s duration suggests their model worker hit its backend timeout (we have model-worker default 30s). We had a short autoscale delay in that AZ at that minute — scaling events show a gap. I'm opening a ticket with infra to check autoscaler logs.

anil_eng: For the customer-facing repro steps, can we ask them to resend a curl with: (1) X-Request-ID header, (2) include -v output, and (3) set X-Forwarded-For if they want geo routing tested. Also request that they keep the exact timestamp. Example to ask them to run: 
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -H "X-Request-ID: req_20250202_0a7f9c-localtest" \
  -H "X-Forwarded-For: 1.2.3.4" -d '{"input":"repro test"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```

sara_support: I'll send that to the customer and ask for the raw -v output. Also requesting a screenshot of the timestamp on their side and whether they were sending long inputs (sequence length) — long prompts increase worker time.

jess_support: Also, can we produce an internal debug bundle for that request id (logs + span dumps + worker metrics) and attach it to the support ticket?

marco_sre: Yes — I'll generate debug bundle. Internal command: 
```
/infra/debug-bundle --request-id req_20250202_0a7f9c --include=logs,spans,worker-metrics --out=/tmp/req_req_20250202_0a7f9c.tgz
```
I'll upload to the ticket under /support/debug-bundles/req_20250202_0a7f9c.tgz and tag @jess_support. Note the bundle will omit any raw auth tokens.

logs-bot: Uploaded debug bundle: https://internal.redwood/support/debug-bundles/req_20250202_0a7f9c.tgz :package: (retention: 90 days).

anil_eng: One more note: if we need to search by client_id or customer API key instead of request_id, use Kibana query: `term: {"api_key_id.keyword":"acct_acme_42"}` and correlate. That helps if request_id was rotated by gateway.

sara_support: I'll relay repro steps to the customer, ask for the curl -v and full header dump, and attach the debug bundle link. Will update ticket when they reply.

jess_support: Great — thanks everyone. If infra confirms autoscaler lag we should follow up on config (lower cooldown) and add a runbook note.

marco_sre: Filing follow-up action in infra backlog: AUTOSCALE-1421.

sara_support: marking thread resolved for now, will reopen if customer provides new evidence. :white_check_mark:
